0: How many bones are in an adult skeleton?
A baby is born with about 300 bones, some of which fuse together as it grows.
1: Which organ pumps blood around the whole body?
It beats about 100,000 times a day.
2: What is the largest organ of the human body?
In an adult, the skin covers nearly 2 m².
3: What is the longest bone in the human body?
The femur, the thigh bone, is about a quarter of a person's height.
4: Which organ does food reach right after the oesophagus?
A layer of mucus protects the stomach wall from its own acid.
5: Which gas from the air do our lungs pass into the blood?
At rest, an adult breathes about 12 to 20 times a minute.
6: In which part of the body is the smallest human bone?
This bone, the stirrup (stapes), is about 3 mm long.
7: A red blood cell lives about 120 days before being recycled.
8: Which organs filter the blood to make urine?
The kidneys filter about 180 litres of fluid a day, almost all of which is reabsorbed.
9: Which iron-containing blood protein binds oxygen?
Blood is bright red when haemoglobin is loaded with oxygen, and darker when it isn't.
10: How many teeth are in a full set of adult teeth?
A child has only 20 baby teeth.
11: Insulin, which controls blood sugar, was first isolated in 1921.
12: How many pairs of chromosomes do most human cells have?
That makes 46 chromosomes in total; egg and sperm cells have only 23.
13: Which part of the eye contains the rods and cones?
Rods let us see in dim light, while cones tell colours apart.
14: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
A year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days.
15: What is the largest planet in the solar system?
More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.
16: How many planets are in the solar system?
Pluto was reclassified as a “dwarf planet” in 2006.
17: Which planet is nicknamed the “Red Planet”?
Its colour comes from iron oxide – in other words, rust – in its soil.
18: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
It happened in July 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission.
19: What is the closest star to Earth?
The Sun alone makes up about 99.8% of the mass of the solar system.
20: Who was the first person to go into space?
His flight, on 12 April 1961, lasted 108 minutes.
21: What is the name of our galaxy?
It contains several hundred billion stars.
22: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
So we always see the Sun as it was about 8 minutes ago.
23: What is the hottest planet in the solar system?
Its thick atmosphere traps heat: its surface is over 460 °C.
24: Roughly how long does the Moon take to orbit the Earth?
It always shows us the same side, because it spins on its axis in the same amount of time.
25: Which planet spins almost lying on its side?
Its axis of rotation is tilted by about 98°.
26: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
In one year, light travels about 9,500 billion km: that's a light-year.
27: What is the largest natural satellite in the solar system?
This moon of Jupiter is bigger than the planet Mercury.
28: What is the largest animal alive today?
It can grow to more than 25 metres long.
29: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
An elephant, a herbivore, can eat more than 100 kg of plants a day.
30: How many legs does a spider have?
Spiders are not insects: insects have 6 legs.
31: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
In return, they release oxygen into the air.
32: What is the fastest land animal?
It can reach about 100 km/h, but only over a few hundred metres.
33: What is a baby frog called?
At first, it breathes through gills, like a fish.
34: What is the only mammal that can truly fly?
The other “flying mammals” can only glide.
35: How many hearts does an octopus have?
Its blood is blue, because it carries oxygen using copper rather than iron.
36: In autumn, as it disappears, it reveals the yellow and orange pigments already present in the leaves.
37: What is the largest bird in the world?
It lays the biggest egg of any living bird.
38: What do we call the change from a caterpillar into a butterfly?
Inside the chrysalis, much of the caterpillar's body is rebuilt.
39: What is the largest fish in the world?
This giant feeds mainly on plankton and is harmless to humans.
40: Which part of a flower produces pollen?
The pistil is the female organ that receives the pollen.
41: Into how many compartments is a cow's stomach divided?
The largest, the rumen, can hold more than 100 litres.
42: What is the highest mountain in the world?
Its summit stands about 8,849 m above sea level.
43: What is the largest ocean in the world?
It alone covers nearly a third of the Earth's surface.
44: What do we call a mountain that can spew out lava?
45: A barometer measures air pressure; an anemometer measures wind speed.
46: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
Antarctica, a cold desert, is even bigger.
47: What is the noise that comes with lightning called?
Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder and divide by 3: that's how far away the storm is in km.
48: About 6 in 10 people live in Asia.
49: Where is the deepest point in the oceans?
It is about 11,000 m deep: Mount Everest would disappear inside it completely.
50: What do we call a scientist who studies volcanoes?
Seismologists, on the other hand, study earthquakes.
51: Which gas is most plentiful in the air?
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air, compared with 21% for oxygen.
52: What is a giant wave caused by an undersea earthquake called?
Out at sea, a tsunami can travel at over 700 km/h while staying almost invisible.
53: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
There, ozone filters out much of the Sun's ultraviolet rays.
54: What was the supercontinent that joined almost all the land together about 250 million years ago?
The continents are still moving today, by a few centimetres a year.
55: What is the main metal in the Earth's core?
At the very centre, the inner core is solid despite a temperature similar to that of the Sun's surface.
56: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
High in the mountains, water boils at a lower temperature because the air pressure is lower.
57: At what temperature does pure water freeze?
Salt water freezes at a lower temperature: that's why roads are salted in winter.
58: Which force makes objects fall to the ground?
On the Moon, gravity is about 6 times weaker than on Earth.
59: What is the chemical formula for water?
Each water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
60: Which of these metals is attracted by a magnet?
Nickel and cobalt are also attracted by magnets.
61: What do we call the change from a solid to a liquid?
That's what happens to an ice cube melting in a glass.
62: Which clear glass object splits white light into colours?
Using prisms, Isaac Newton showed that white light is a mixture of colours.
63: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
Au comes from the Latin aurum, meaning “gold”.
64: It is also the most abundant element in the Universe.
65: Which scientist set out the law of universal gravitation?
Newton himself said he was inspired by a falling apple.
66: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
Below 7, a solution is acidic; above 7, it is basic.
67: Which scientist won two Nobel Prizes in two different sciences?
She won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.
68: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
Gallium, meanwhile, melts in your hand, at around 30 °C.
69: What is the unit of force?
A force of 1 newton is roughly the weight of a 100 g apple.
